fields.description:
## Context / Problem

Stores that already exist — including client deployments, not just this one — have no
`.bridge_state/projects.json` and no `bridge_project` on any ticket. Without a migration those stores
would read every ticket as having an absent project, and there would be no recorded legacy default
for the resolver to fall back to, so a store that syncs perfectly today would stop syncing on upgrade.

## Prerequisites (substrate this story builds on)

The projects-mapping substrate this migration seeds and reads is delivered by cited dependencies, not
by this story:

- `[rebar:c927-0a68]` — the bridge-projects mapping store `projects_store.py`: the
  `.bridge_state/projects.json` record (`{version, legacy_default, projects}`), `load_mapping`,
  the `Mapping` dataclass, the tri-state resolver `resolve_project` (absent field → `legacy_default`;
  `""` → `None`; key → verbatim), and the mutation helpers `set_project`/`read_projects`.
- `[rebar:67f9-4a07]` — registers `multi-project-bridge` in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`
  (`src/rebar/_store/compat.py:63`), so a store may stamp it and still pass its own compat gate.

`Backend.project` (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py:598-605`, the effective
write/create scope) is pre-existing. Both `[rebar:c927-0a68]` and `[rebar:67f9-4a07]` are already
recorded `depends_on` edges of this ticket.

## Approach

Ship the migration as ensure units on the existing idempotent registry
(`src/rebar/_store/ensures.py`, `REGISTRY_IDS` at `:66`, `_registry()` at `:82`), which is rebar's
sanctioned seam: `docs/migrations.md:40-56` describes adding a unit, and the ordered School-A ledger
is explicitly not built (`docs/migrations.md:14-16`). Units run at init/re-init, `fsck --repair`, and
MCP boot (`docs/migrations.md:57-65`), so a client store converges without any operator action.

**The migration writes no ticket events.** A unit emitting an EDIT per ticket would be a four-figure
event write under the store write lock on a store this size, and the MCP-boot entry point runs the
sweep on a deliberately short lock budget and skips when contended (`docs/migrations.md:63-65`) — so
an event-writing migration would silently skip at one of its three entry points and converge
unpredictably. Instead the unit records `legacy_default` once in the mapping, and the tri-state
resolver `resolve_project` `[rebar:c927-0a68]` treats every ticket with an absent field as belonging
to it. One small write migrates the whole store.

Two units, both check-then-act and both safe to re-run:

1. **Seed the mapping.** If `.bridge_state/projects.json` `[rebar:c927-0a68]` is absent, write it with
   `legacy_default` and a single `projects` entry taken from the backend's configured project
   (`Backend.project`, `_backend.py:598-605`). If the record already exists, return `ok` and write
   nothing. Tree-check the committed `tickets:.bridge_state/projects.json` blob before committing so a
   converged store makes zero git commits, as `docs/migrations.md:45-46` requires of commit units.
2. **Stamp the capability (idempotent convergence).** When — and only when — the mapping holds more
   than one project, add `multi-project-bridge` to `.store-compat.json`'s `required_capabilities`; a
   single-project store is never stamped and stays usable by older binaries. This is a level-triggered
   ensure unit: it is deliberately **decoupled from how the store became multi-project**. The seed
   unit above only ever produces a **one-project** mapping, so this unit never fires as a consequence
   of the same sweep's seed — it fires on a *later* sweep, once an operator has added a second project
   to the mapping (via `set_project` `[rebar:c927-0a68]` or a direct mapping edit). No sibling story
   owns a write-time capability stamp (7032 only *documents* the token's meaning), so this ensure unit
   is the single authoritative stamp: a store that reaches a multi-project mapping cannot be left
   unstamped, because the next init/`fsck --repair`/MCP-boot sweep converges it. The
   `multi-project-bridge` token is already registered in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`
   (`compat.py:63`) `[rebar:67f9-4a07]`, so a stamped store still passes its own `check_store_compat`
   on this binary — this story makes **no** edit to `compat.py`, and a test asserts the two-project
   stamped store passes the gate (guarding a future rename that would fail the store closed against the
   very binary that stamped it).

Ids are new and never reused, per `docs/migrations.md:50-51`.

**Where the unit bodies live.** The existing six units are implemented in `src/rebar/_commands/init.py`
(for example `_store_compat_unit` at `:509`) and referenced from `_registry()`
(`src/rebar/_store/ensures.py:82`). This story places the two new unit bodies in their own
`src/rebar/_store/project_ensures.py` rather than in `init.py`. `init.py` measures **758 lines** — it
has ~42 lines of headroom under the hard 800-line module-size gate
(`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), so a separate module is a **cohesion** choice, not a size-forced
one: the projects-mapping migration is a distinct concern from init's `.gitignore`/`.gitattributes`
content constants, a dedicated module keeps `init.py` from drifting toward the cap, and it groups the
two related units together. Because `_registry()` maps an id to any callable, `ensures.py`
(257 lines) gains only its two registry entries.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/project_ensures.py` (new) — both unit bodies
- `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py` — two `REGISTRY_IDS` entries and two `_registry()` mappings
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_ensures.py` — update the hardcoded `expected` id-set literal in
  `test_registry_id_set_is_frozen` (`:57`, currently the six existing ids) to add the two new ids, so
  the registry-agreement test passes with the new units
- `docs/migrations.md` — document the two new units and the meaning of the `multi-project-bridge`
  capability token for other binaries/operators (it gates `.store-compat.json` compatibility)
- `tests/integration/test_ensure_project_mapping.py` (new) — the behavioural oracle below

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's git row — real temporary git repositories and refs — because the
units commit to the `tickets` branch and the zero-commit-when-converged property is only observable
against real refs.

- Happy path: sweeping a store with no mapping creates one whose `legacy_default` equals the
  configured backend project, and every existing ticket resolves to it via `resolve_project`.
- The load-bearing assertion: the sweep writes **zero ticket events**. Assert the store's event count
  and the set of event files are identical before and after — this is what distinguishes this design
  from an EDIT-per-ticket migration.
- Idempotence: a second sweep on a converged store returns `ok` for both units and makes zero new git
  commits (assert the branch tip SHA is unchanged, not merely that no error was raised).
- Conditional stamp, as a contrast pair: a one-project mapping leaves `required_capabilities` empty; a
  two-project mapping adds exactly `multi-project-bridge`. The one-project half proves the stamp is
  genuinely conditional rather than unconditional.
- Compat-gate safety: a two-project store that has stamped `multi-project-bridge` still passes
  `check_store_compat` on this binary — proves the stamp does not fail the store closed against the
  binary that wrote it.
- Failure path: a unit raising is recorded as `failed` and does not abort the sweep or the caller, per
  the registry's skip-and-continue contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A store with no mapping gains one whose `legacy_default` equals the configured backend project;
      checked by a real-git test reading the seeded record.
- [ ] Every pre-existing ticket (absent `bridge_project`) resolves to that legacy default via
      `resolve_project` `[rebar:c927-0a68]`; checked by the same test.
- [ ] The sweep writes zero ticket events; checked by asserting the event file set is identical before
      and after the sweep.
- [ ] A second sweep returns `ok` for both units; checked by the returned outcome statuses.
- [ ] A second sweep leaves the tickets-branch tip SHA unchanged; checked by comparing the SHA across
      two sweeps.
- [ ] A one-project mapping leaves `required_capabilities` empty; checked by a real-git test.
- [ ] A two-project mapping adds exactly `multi-project-bridge` to `required_capabilities`; checked by
      a real-git test.
- [ ] A two-project store that has stamped `multi-project-bridge` still passes `check_store_compat` on
      this binary; checked by a test invoking the compat gate.
- [ ] The two new unit ids are added to REGISTRY_IDS and mapped in `_registry()`, AND added to the
      hardcoded `expected` literal in `test_registry_id_set_is_frozen`
      (`tests/interfaces/store/test_ensures.py:57`), so that registry-agreement test passes.
- [ ] A unit that raises is recorded `failed` and does not abort the sweep or its caller; checked by
      monkeypatching a raising unit into `_registry()`.
